patterns.name: Standard (CLM prefix)
patterns.note: Format: CLM_<creativename>_<cohortname>_<channel-token>_date/month. Channel-token is 'push' for Push and 'Emailer' for Email - separate from the API's 'channel' field which returns 'PUSH'/'EMAIL'. Day accepts either a leading zero (08) or not (8).

patterns.name: ADH client (SMS/Email/WhatsApp)
patterns.note: Format: ADH_<BrandName>_<Creative>_<Cohort[_Region]>_OMNI_<Channel>_WK<week>_<DDMMYYYY>. OMNI is a fixed literal segment (ignored for meaning, but required in the name). Channel token is 'SMS'/'EMAIL'/'WA' (WA = WhatsApp) - separate from the API's 'channel' field which returns 'WHATSAPP'. Confirmed against 3 real examples (SMS, Email, WhatsApp) - flag if a legitimately-named campaign from this client ever gets rejected, since this was built from field descriptions rather than a large sample.

naming_convention.note: A campaign passes if its name matches ANY pattern above - lets multiple clients/teams with different naming conventions share this same QA tool without conflicting.

tags_check.note: Generic fallback: flags campaigns with no tags at all. Overridden per client+channel by client_channel_rules.<CLIENT>.<CHANNEL> when configured - either tags_must_match_name_segments (KFC PUSH: derives the expected cohort/creative names from the campaign name itself and checks each shows up as a tag, since MoEngage's tag categories aren't in the API response - only the flat tag text is) or the simpler required_tags_contains (literal keyword match).

segment_sanity.note: Flags all-user campaigns missing an approval tag, and flags targeted campaigns that somehow have zero included audience filters (likely a targeting mistake).

content_check.note: Channel-specific, meaningful checks rather than just presence/absence. PUSH: per-platform title/message length limits (device truncation), title==message duplicate detection, placeholder-copy detection, and (if you list them) which platforms (android/ios/web) must be present. EMAIL: subject length range, preview text not duplicating the subject, from/reply-to address format, from_address domain against approved_from_domains (leave empty to skip), placeholder-copy detection. SMS: real GSM segment-length math (160 single-segment / 153 per concatenated segment) so silent multi-segment sends get flagged, not just 'is there text'. WHATSAPP: placeholder-copy detection plus a best-effort template_name check (require_template_name) - the exact WhatsApp content payload shape wasn't available to confirm, so adjust _check_whatsapp_content in moengage_qa_agent.py if your field names differ. Any channel not listed above (or with expected_platforms/approved_from_domains left empty) falls back to length-only checks so nothing breaks before you tune these.

control_group_check.note: Flags campaigns where neither global nor campaign-level control group is enabled - meaning there's no way to measure this campaign's incremental impact. Disable this if most of your campaigns intentionally skip control groups.

conversion_goal_check.note: standard_goals_by_client is keyed by client key, matching clients_config.json. KFC: 3 standard goals ('purchase' primary/revenue, 'registrationFinish' + 'registration_complete' secondary). HOAD_IND/HOAD_USA/HOAD_UAE/ANDGD_IND: 2 standard goals ('Order_Summary' primary/revenue, 'LineItem_Purchase' secondary) - identical structure across all 4 HOAD/ANDGD dashboards, only revenue_currency differs (INR/USD/AED) per the confirmed currency-per-dashboard mapping. WESTSIDE has no entry yet, so campaigns for that client fall back to the plain presence-only checks (require_at_least_one_goal / require_exactly_one_primary_goal) below - add a WESTSIDE array here (same shape) once its standard goals are defined. Set flag_extra_goals to true to also flag any goal beyond the standard list, for a client that has one configured.

delivery_controls_check.note: bypass_dnd flagging is OFF - it's intentional/standard on this team's Fixed-timing campaigns. Set flag_if_bypass_dnd to true if you ever want it back (e.g. to catch it being on for a non-time-critical campaign by mistake). Generic fallback only - overridden per client+channel by client_channel_rules.<CLIENT>.<CHANNEL>.delivery_controls when configured (e.g. KFC PUSH requires an exact campaign_throttle_rpm of 100000, not just 'non-zero').

pending_verification.note: Only these 3 remain unconfirmed - they simply don't appear anywhere in a real KFC PUSH campaign JSON that has them in their default/off state (Precompute audience, Campaign audience limit, and Background update targeting were all off/unchecked in the screenshots), so it's not yet known what key(s) MoEngage adds when they're turned ON. If a campaign that has any of these enabled ever gets flagged as a false pass, dump that campaign's raw JSON (python3 moengage_qa_agent.py --dump-raw) and share it to wire these in.

client_channel_rules.note: Per-client, per-channel overrides/additions on top of the generic checks above - keyed by client key (matching the Client Name dropdown) then channel (matching the API's channel value, e.g. PUSH/EMAIL/SMS/WHATSAPP). KFC/PUSH, KFC/EMAIL, and HOAD_IND|HOAD_USA|HOAD_UAE|ANDGD_IND EMAIL are filled in so far; add more client/channel blocks the same way as they're defined. See check_client_channel_rules in moengage_qa_agent.py for how each key is used. Note content.email is intentionally NOT set for the HOAD/ANDGD dashboards (unlike KFC) - per instructions, sender domain/reply-to/etc only need to be checked for presence there, which the generic content_check.email defaults already do. Confirmed: conversion_goal_attribution_hours_required is 7 for ALL channels of HOAD_IND/HOAD_USA/HOAD_UAE/ANDGD_IND (not just EMAIL) - carry this same value=7 into their WA/SMS/RCS blocks when those are added.

utm_required.note: Disabled per request. Re-enable (set enabled: true) if you want this back.

utm_mismatch_check.note: Disabled per request. Re-enable if you want to catch drift between campaign-level UTM template and UTMs baked into body links.

link_check.note: Disabled per request - was generating noise from LinkedIn/TikTok blocking bot requests. Re-enable if useful, ideally with a domain ignore-list for social platforms.
